candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Explain how leadership walkrounds should be used to support patient safety.

options.A: Invite frontline staff to discuss safety concerns and ensure concerns receive structured follow-up.
options.B: Use the rounds only to observe staff silently and avoid discussing problems.
options.C: Collect concerns but avoid follow-up so staff remain independent.
options.D: Limit the rounds to reviewing financial performance with no discussion of patient safety.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ describes leadership walkrounds as management visits to clinical areas that engage frontline workers in discussion of safety concerns. Their value depends on meaningful follow-up; concerns raised without response can make the rounds a visibility exercise rather than an effective safety intervention.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Leadership walkrounds engage frontline staff about safety concerns and require follow-up to be meaningful.
candidate.source_document_title: The Role of Leadership in Improving Safety
candidate.source_locator: Leadership walkrounds—engage frontline workers in safety discussions; concerns should receive prompt follow-up
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, PSNet
candidate.stem: A nurse manager conducts leadership walkrounds on a patient-care unit. Which approach best supports the safety purpose of these rounds?
